requirements.risk: A green test run can conceal missing, stale, skipped or unrelated acceptance coverage.

scenarios.given: Reviewed positive and negative fixtures with exact assertions
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: No alignment errors

scenarios.given: Missing or empty acceptance/test data
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: Reject missing manifests, empty requirements and empty discovered suites

scenarios.given: Absent negative coverage, imaginary tests, unmapped tests or duplicate identities
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: Reject incomplete or ambiguous scenario/test mappings

scenarios.given: Required tests use skip decorators, runtime skip or expected failure
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: Reject every skipped or expected-failure required test

scenarios.given: A test loses its assertion, becomes vacuous, or weakens an exact assertion after review
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: Reject absent/vacuous assertions or a stale source review

scenarios.given: Scenario mappings are swapped or the expected outcome is weakened after review
scenarios.when: Check traceability
scenarios.then: Reject missing/mismatched semantic review or a changed scenario

requirements.risk: API failures can expose request details or an unhealthy API can appear available.

scenarios.given: No authenticated session or database access
scenarios.when: GET /api/health/
scenarios.then: 200 with exactly status ok and Cache-Control no-store

scenarios.given: A caller attempts to mutate liveness
scenarios.when: POST /api/health/
scenarios.then: 405 JSON method_not_allowed and Allow GET

scenarios.given: An unknown private-looking path or untrusted host
scenarios.when: Request the API
scenarios.then: Generic JSON 404 or 400 with no path/host reflection; errors are not cached

requirements.risk: A client could forge identity, read another user's session or mutate a session across origins.

scenarios.given: Two synthetic Django users with separate authenticated sessions
scenarios.when: Read the session, including attempts to supply another identity
scenarios.then: The body identifies only the authenticated user as a string ID; sessions remain separate and responses private

scenarios.given: Anonymous, inactive or forged-cookie client
scenarios.when: Read /api/session/
scenarios.then: 401 authentication_required without a CSRF bootstrap for anonymous clients

scenarios.given: A signed-in user supplies valid CSRF for an unsupported session write
scenarios.when: POST /api/session/
scenarios.then: 405 with Allow GET

scenarios.given: An authenticated session and valid same-origin CSRF token
scenarios.when: POST /api/session/logout/
scenarios.then: 200 signed_out, no-store, and subsequent session read is 401

scenarios.given: An authenticated session with absent CSRF, foreign origin, or GET
scenarios.when: Attempt logout
scenarios.then: 403 CSRF failure or 405 method refusal, preserving the session

scenarios.given: Secure configuration with authenticated session bootstrap
scenarios.when: Read /api/session/
scenarios.then: Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, nosniff and frame denial

requirements.risk: A host could start with missing secrets, permissive hosts, debug or insecure cookie defaults.

scenarios.given: A private synthetic key and exact production host
scenarios.when: Import settings in a fresh process
scenarios.then: Debug off, only the configured host, both cookies secure

scenarios.given: An explicit local development opt-in and synthetic key
scenarios.when: Import settings without a host override
scenarios.then: Only loopback hosts, debug off and local HTTP cookie settings

scenarios.given: A missing/short key, absent production hosts or wildcard host
scenarios.when: Import settings in a fresh process
scenarios.then: Startup fails with a generic configuration instruction and no key reflection

requirements.risk: Passing a partial/empty/skipped test run or importing app code before alignment could make the gate misleading.

scenarios.given: One successfully executed required test
scenarios.when: Classify the test result
scenarios.then: Exit code 0

scenarios.given: Zero execution, runtime skip or expected failure
scenarios.when: Classify the test result
scenarios.then: Exit code 1

scenarios.given: Misaligned coverage or non-test Django settings
scenarios.when: Run the scoped pipeline with Django import deliberately unavailable
scenarios.then: Return failure before importing Django or executing app tests

requirements.risk: A development asset host could leak private files or unintentionally become a production surface.

scenarios.given: Explicit local development with a trusted synthetic build
scenarios.when: GET the shell and asset
scenarios.then: Serve the exact built files; shell is not cached

scenarios.given: Non-development mode, missing build or asset traversal
scenarios.when: Request local UI content
scenarios.then: Non-development and traversal return404 without private contents; missing build returns503

requirements.risk: Stale or private file data could be presented as a new deployed build, or a read endpoint could accept writes.

scenarios.given: A generated build manifest with a valid hash and extra synthetic private-looking data
scenarios.when: Anonymous GET /api/version/
scenarios.then: 200 with only the exact built hash and no-store; no extra manifest fields are exposed

scenarios.given: Missing, broken, oversized, wrong-schema or malformed build metadata, or an attempted version write
scenarios.when: Read or POST the version endpoint
scenarios.then: Invalid metadata returns generic503/no-store; writes return405 with Allow GET

scenarios.when: Initialize, create/prompt/read a session, correlate simultaneous replies, handle server requests, and stop or fail the connection
scenarios.then: Owned sessions and replies route exactly while permission requests cancel and unsupported calls error; foreign authority, malformed/oversized/failed peers and deadlines fail closed without private diagnostics or retries

scenarios.given: An application-owned ACP client with a fixed trusted workspace and immutable user/account scope, exercised with a synthetic bidirectional subprocess peer

scenarios.then: Owned sessions and replies route exactly while permission requests cancel and unsupported calls error; foreign authority, malformed/oversized/failed peers and deadlines fail closed without private diagnostics or retries

scenarios.when: Initialize the real entry, exercise a session using the published CodexDriver with a synthetic transport, or attempt foreign workspace/MCP input
scenarios.then: The locked runtime initializes and standard chunks complete an owned fixture turn; foreign configuration constructs no driver and shutdown verdicts remain distinct from process exit

scenarios.given: The exact installed published ACP package, a trusted synthetic account/home/workspace profile, and the application Python/Node bootstrap

requirements.risk: A browser could choose another user's provider profile, launch privileged workers, leak setup paths/diagnostics, or confuse a transport handshake with subscription readiness.

scenarios.given: Two Django-authenticated users with server-owned account metadata and synthetic isolated transport-check storage
scenarios.when: List owned accounts, request or read a transport check, forge identity/configuration, or encounter failures
scenarios.then: Only the active server-session owner can inspect/check their metadata; the real published host initializes with zero providers, records the exact transport outcome and never claims login/provider readiness; all authority, CSRF, input, rate and diagnostic failures fail closed

scenarios.given: Two Django-authenticated users with server-owned account metadata and synthetic isolated transport-check storage
scenarios.when: List owned accounts, request or read a transport check, forge identity/configuration, or encounter failures
scenarios.then: Only the active server-session owner can inspect/check their metadata; the real published host initializes with zero providers, records the exact transport outcome and never claims login/provider readiness; all authority, CSRF, input, rate and diagnostic failures fail closed

requirements.risk: A partial, stale or exit-zero-only check could publish misleading all-green evidence.

scenarios.given: A fixed bootstrap stage sequence with synthetic child evidence and exact candidate snapshots
scenarios.when: Execute all required gates or inject missing evidence, failures or source changes
scenarios.then: A complete unchanged candidate passes in alignment-first/browser-last order with exact build evidence

scenarios.given: A fixed bootstrap stage sequence with synthetic child evidence and exact candidate snapshots
scenarios.when: Execute all required gates or inject missing evidence, failures or source changes
scenarios.then: Failure, incomplete evidence or changed source invalidates the run and prevents subsequent stage effects without diagnostic leakage

requirements.risk: Dependency checks could reject legitimate npm bundles or accept unapproved installed code and unsafe registries.

scenarios.given: Synthetic exact manifest, npm lock and installed package directory
scenarios.when: Check ordinary/bundled published closure or inject extra, unpinned, mismatched or unsafe entries
scenarios.then: Exact installed closure with integrity-covered optional bundles passes

scenarios.given: Synthetic exact manifest, npm lock and installed package directory
scenarios.when: Check ordinary/bundled published closure or inject extra, unpinned, mismatched or unsafe entries
scenarios.then: Unapproved installed packages, unverified bundles and unsafe dependency inputs fail

requirements.risk: Hosted diagnostics could leak child paths/cookies or mistake malformed cleanup evidence for verified cleanup.

scenarios.given: Child failure metadata containing a fixed stage code or arbitrary diagnostic fields
scenarios.when: Create public-safe failure evidence
scenarios.then: Only zero checks, an allowed stage code and exact boolean cleanup survive

scenarios.given: Child failure metadata containing a fixed stage code or arbitrary diagnostic fields
scenarios.when: Create public-safe failure evidence
scenarios.then: Arbitrary diagnostics and nonboolean or unknown cleanup claims never appear as verified evidence

requirements.risk: Login can leak credentials, accept forged identity, permit brute force or retain invalidated session authority.

scenarios.given: An anonymous same-origin browser
scenarios.when: GET the CSRF bootstrap
scenarios.then: Return only an uncached nonempty CSRF token, without a redirect or private identity.

scenarios.given: A provisioned active member and existing browser session
scenarios.when: Authenticate with a real password and then logout
scenarios.then: Rotate session and CSRF authority; bind the correct user; logout invalidates a captured old session cookie.

scenarios.given: A login read, missing token or foreign origin
scenarios.when: Attempt authentication
scenarios.then: Refuse GET with 405/Allow POST and no redirect; reject CSRF/origin failures with 403 without authenticating.

scenarios.given: Unknown, wrong-password, inactive or unprovisioned users
scenarios.when: Attempt a real login
scenarios.then: Return identical generic 401 invalid_credentials with no authenticated session.

scenarios.given: Malformed, duplicate-key, role/tenant-forged or overbudget JSON
scenarios.when: POST login
scenarios.then: Reject invalid schema with 400 and overbudget payloads with 413; create no authenticated session.

scenarios.given: An already authenticated principal
scenarios.when: Try to login as another principal
scenarios.then: Return 409 already_signed_in and retain the original identity.

scenarios.given: Five wrong-password attempts using fresh browser sessions
scenarios.when: Try a sixth login with the correct password
scenarios.then: Return 429 login_rate_limited with Retry-After 900 and persist no plaintext username in the attempt budget.

requirements.risk: Client hints, roles or stale membership can cross installation/user authority and expose another user account history.

scenarios.given: A provisioned preparer and forged user/tenant/role hints
scenarios.when: Read workspace context and attempt another install row
scenarios.then: Return the server installation and preparer permission oracle; database rejects a second installation.

scenarios.given: Two users logged in with real passwords and one private account/history
scenarios.when: Read each user account and transport history
scenarios.then: Administrator sees no foreign account and receives generic 404 for foreign history; original owner retains their history.

scenarios.given: A viewer with their own account and forged administrator hints
scenarios.when: POST a transport check
scenarios.then: Return 403 permission_denied with no created check; own account metadata remains readable.

scenarios.given: A logged-in member whose membership is disabled server-side
scenarios.when: Read session, workspace or provider accounts without logging in again
scenarios.then: Every protected read returns generic 403 workspace_access_denied immediately.

requirements.risk: Unprovisioned/passwordless principals could gain workspace authority or a setup process could replace passwords.

scenarios.given: A trusted console operator and an existing active password user
scenarios.when: Grant explicit administrator membership
scenarios.then: Persist the explicit enabled role under the sole installation without changing or storing a plaintext password.

scenarios.given: Unknown, inactive or passwordless users
scenarios.when: Attempt console provisioning
scenarios.then: Refuse all candidates without creating an installation or membership.

requirements.risk: Genie HTTPS termination can reject legitimate login; broad origin or forwarded-header trust could weaken CSRF.

scenarios.given: Explicit local Genie mode with maipa.gen in exact allowed hosts
scenarios.when: Load the real settings and authenticate with HTTPS Origin over loopback HTTP proxy transport
scenarios.then: Trust exactly https://maipa.gen and authenticate the correct member with CSRF; no forwarded-header trust is required.

scenarios.given: Production mode or an unrelated local hostname
scenarios.when: Load settings
scenarios.then: No automatic Genie CSRF trusted origin is added.

requirements.risk: A provider process or detached descendant could read server/other-user data, mutate trusted code, outlive its owner or execute under stale account authority.

scenarios.given: Existing synthetic assigned, foreign-user, server and public-code files, plus an unrestricted control
scenarios.when: Run a real Node worker and its real Node descendant under native isolation
scenarios.then: Both restricted processes read assigned/public code but receive EACCES/EPERM for foreign/server files; assigned writes work, code writes fail; job empty and profile removed.

scenarios.given: An actual running root and detached Node descendant, with process handles opened before termination
scenarios.when: Kill the worker or its owning server process
scenarios.then: Both observed process handles become signalled, without killing arbitrary PIDs; native job empties and profile is cleaned after death.

scenarios.given: A foreign immutable user/account scope or overlapping writable parent/public-code layout
scenarios.when: Attempt a native launch
scenarios.then: Refuse before any child starts; a writable root cannot contain immutable runtime code.

scenarios.given: A valid server-owned member/provider account and installed published Prism ACP package
scenarios.when: Execute the actual application transport check
scenarios.then: Return real Windows AppContainer verification, empty native job and zero provider sessions, after published-host initialization/shutdown.

scenarios.given: An account object captured before membership revocation or reassignment
scenarios.when: Call the real transport function
scenarios.then: Refuse revoked membership and stale original-owner authority before launching a worker.

scenarios.given: An actual isolated Node process keeps running without reading its native input pipe
scenarios.when: Send a 64KiB ACP request with a 0.2 second deadline
scenarios.then: The application deadline ends the blocked write with its fixed AcpError before the 3 second test watchdog; the native job is empty and its profile is removed.

scenarios.given: Parent process carries synthetic secret and runtime injection variables, and one actual worker runs under an immutable scope
scenarios.when: Inspect the real child environment, try foreign revocation, then revoke its own scope
scenarios.then: No forbidden variable is inherited; foreign revocation fails without ending the observed process; own-scope revocation ends its handle and empties the native job.

scenarios.given: Two distinct user/account AppContainers with both private workspace ACLs present and a shared immutable runtime
scenarios.when: Launch both real workers and their Node descendants, then observe both root handles alive
scenarios.then: Each root and descendant reads its own file and shared code but receives permission denial for the other assigned workspace and synthetic server file; both live handles end and jobs/profiles clean up.

requirements.risk: Private server files or patched runtime bytes could be staged; junctions or cleanup could escape the owned worker root.

scenarios.given: The installed actual published ACP runtime and Node binary, plus an unrelated synthetic file beside the owned worker root
scenarios.when: Prepare and close a real runtime capsule
scenarios.then: Every staged package/host/manifest byte and Node binary matches the unchanged source; supervisor exists, writable directories start empty; cleanup removes only the owned child.

scenarios.given: An actual freshly created Windows junction points at a synthetic target
scenarios.when: Use the junction as runtime or a worker-root ancestor
scenarios.then: Refuse before creating files in the target; remove the junction itself after the test.

requirements.risk: An opaque hosted backend failure can stall diagnosis; printing raw exceptions can disclose private paths, data or credentials.

scenarios.given: A known reviewed test raises a native error with a fixed phase/code and a private message
scenarios.when: Build public failure evidence
scenarios.then: Retain the known test identifier, allowlisted phase/code and bounded exception kinds; exclude every exception message.

scenarios.given: An unknown identifier, private metadata, cyclic exception context or untrusted extra report fields
scenarios.when: Collect result and CI failure metadata
scenarios.then: Unknown names are redacted, context traversal terminates, arbitrary fields/messages never escape, and real assertion failures remain failures.

requirements.risk: A native browser may need Windows startup paths absent in scrubbed CI; diagnostics must not leak credentials or raw browser text.

scenarios.given: A scrubbed CI environment plus OS-resolved startup paths, private credentials and injection flags
scenarios.when: Build the dedicated browser child environment
scenarios.then: Use authoritative Windows profile/system paths and ambient tool/temp paths; forward no credentials/injection fields and do not change the caller environment.

scenarios.given: A fixed browser-launch phase/state with numeric exit and allowlisted spawn code, plus private stderr
scenarios.when: Build public launch-failure evidence
scenarios.then: Retain only bounded fixed startup state, numeric exit and known spawn code; discard every child text field.

scenarios.given: Private/unknown state/code metadata and a boolean masquerading as an exit number
scenarios.when: Build public launch evidence
scenarios.then: Discard all untrusted optional fields while preserving fixed failure phase and verified cleanup.

requirements.risk: Inferred, stale, unscoped or overwritten client facts can contaminate later financial conclusions.

scenarios.given: A provisioned preparer and synthetic engagement with two entities
scenarios.when: Record every typed fact with evidence and dates
scenarios.then: Every exact value, false, reference and date round trips; entities remain separately identified

scenarios.given: Unknown tax facts and a known false completeness assertion
scenarios.when: Record LLC legal form and later explicit unknown completeness
scenarios.then: False remains known false; LLC populates neither tax classification nor elections; unknown uses null

scenarios.given: Bounded original assertion, future assertion and backdated correction
scenarios.when: Read boundary dates and stored history
scenarios.then: Only effective assertions apply; half-open intervals select correct values and preserve original evidence and recorder

scenarios.given: An assertion ends at an explicit exclusive date
scenarios.when: Read immediately before and at expiry
scenarios.then: The expired value becomes unknown rather than implicitly carrying forward

scenarios.given: An existing entity revision and captured fact row
scenarios.when: Submit stale version and attempt direct instance mutation/deletion
scenarios.then: 409 conflict leaves one original revision and unchanged entity version; instance edits and deletes are refused

scenarios.given: Two real conclusion records depend on different known facts
scenarios.when: Append a replacement legal-form assertion
scenarios.then: Only the dependent legal conclusion becomes stale with invalidation time; currency conclusion remains current and original dependency survives

scenarios.given: Stale, unknown, foreign, future-inapplicable or empty fact dependencies
scenarios.when: Attempt to record a current conclusion
scenarios.then: Every invalid dependency is refused and no conclusion is recorded

scenarios.given: Invalid null/state/key/version/date/evidence/typed decimal/contact or forged-owner input
scenarios.when: Record an assertion
scenarios.then: 400 generic invalid_request for every case; no revision or entity version change

scenarios.given: A preparer owns an engagement and another active user is administrator
scenarios.when: Read or mutate through forged owner/install/role hints
scenarios.then: Foreign list is empty and details/history/writes are generic404; owner retains access

scenarios.given: Current role becomes viewer then membership is revoked; anonymous and cross-CSRF callers exist
scenarios.when: Read or attempt writes and forged creation
scenarios.then: Viewer can read own records but cannot write; revocation/anonymous/CSRF/owner injection are denied without new records

scenarios.given: Malformed/duplicate/nonfinite/oversized JSON, unsupported methods and invalid temporal/cursor input
scenarios.when: Call real intake routes then paginate history
scenarios.then: Requests fail generically with400/413/405; valid bounded cursor returns only older revisions

requirements.risk: Anonymous install takeover, duplicate admins, lost/private setup progress or fake financial/provider configuration.

scenarios.given: A pristine database and local operator code
scenarios.when: Read first-run status
scenarios.then: Offer setup without disclosing the code or creating users.

scenarios.given: A pristine installation and matching strong credentials/code
scenarios.when: Claim and replay setup, including after membership disablement
scenarios.then: Create one hashed administrator and rotated session; close setup permanently and reject another claim.

scenarios.given: Invalid code, weak/mismatched passwords or untrusted fields
scenarios.when: Attempt first-run administrator creation
scenarios.then: Reject every invalid request without creating users/install; a subsequent valid request succeeds.

scenarios.given: Missing CSRF or missing local operator-code file
scenarios.when: POST setup or try to read the private file over HTTP
scenarios.then: Reject CSRF, hide private files and fail closed without the local code.

scenarios.given: An existing user or existing installation
scenarios.when: Read and attempt anonymous setup
scenarios.then: Setup stays closed and POST returns conflict.

scenarios.given: A real signed-in member
scenarios.when: Reply, sign out and sign in again
scenarios.then: Resume the saved next prompt and accepted reply; never claim a provider is connected.

scenarios.given: A reviewed account setup draft
scenarios.when: Confirm once and replay the stale confirmation
scenarios.then: Save real owned entity, explicit dated currency/basis and display name once; reject stale replay.

scenarios.given: Two replies at the same setup revision and an object masquerading as an answer
scenarios.when: Submit conflicting and malformed answers
scenarios.then: Reject stale and invalid replies without changing accepted draft.

scenarios.given: Two real members with separate sessions
scenarios.when: Read the other account and then revoke membership
scenarios.then: Keep setup private, reject an old browser tab reply after the signed-in account changes, and deny both reads and writes after revocation.

scenarios.given: A user choosing to defer financial setup
scenarios.when: Confirm the profile and later resume account setup
scenarios.then: Keep the profile, create no financial records and resume from workspace selection with provider setup still required.

scenarios.given: A read-only member
scenarios.when: Attempt financial setup and confirm profile
scenarios.then: Permit only own profile; no finance records or role escalation.

scenarios.given: An owned entity changed independently after setup selection
scenarios.when: Confirm stale setup, reset, then try entity selection as a viewer
scenarios.then: Reject stale finance changes atomically and unauthorized entity selection; allow explicit draft reset.

scenarios.given: Anonymous, missing-CSRF, duplicate/unknown JSON fields or oversized data
scenarios.when: Read or write account setup
scenarios.then: Reject each invalid request and retain setup revision zero.

requirements.risk: Readable local pairing code or simultaneous anonymous claims create multiple administrators.

scenarios.given: A pristine install using the actual local launcher preparation
scenarios.when: Generate and prepare the code repeatedly, then configure the installation
scenarios.then: Create a stable 64-hex random code with a protected owner/System-only Windows DACL or 0600 Unix mode, and create no code for an existing install.

scenarios.given: Two separate real database connections and synchronized HTTP clients with the same valid local code
scenarios.when: Race administrator creation and then replay
scenarios.then: At most one racing request succeeds; transient SQLite lock failures are retryable and final durable state has exactly one administrator with bootstrap closed.
